title: How do we write these answers as mixed fractions?
description: Four multiplications of a whole number and a fraction are done the same way as the example in the book, and each answer is then written as a mixed fraction by dividing. The video ends by checking each answer back into pieces.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiply the whole number into the top, keep the pieces, then divide the top by the bottom to find the whole numbers and the left over. Watch for students who write the left over as the bottom number.

source: Multiply and then convert it into a mixed fraction: 7 × 3/5, 4 × 1/3, 9/7 × 6, 13/11 × 6
video_script.why: The child has multiplied a whole number by a fraction and now meets answers larger than one whole, which are written as a whole number and a fraction.
video_script.substitution: Twenty one fifths fills four bars of five pieces and leaves one piece, so a whole number times a fraction can be read as whole bars and pieces left over.
video_script.anchor: Four multiplications of a whole number and a fraction: write each answer as a mixed fraction.
video_script.payoff_line: Four and one fifth, one and one third, seven and five sevenths, seven and one eleventh

final_answer.spoken: four and one fifth, one and one third, seven and five sevenths, seven and one eleventh

video_script.fraction_reading: three fifths, twenty one fifths, four thirds, nine sevenths, fifty four sevenths, thirteen elevenths, seventy eight elevenths
video_script.design: One idea: multiply the whole number into the top, then divide to find whole bars and pieces left over. A bar cut into equal pieces is the anchor; the four multiplications are written in the working band one by one.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; the four multiplications 7 × 3/5, 4 × 1/3, 9/7 × 6, 13/11 × 6 written in a row; a question mark after each

marks.scene: the small title card From your book appears
marks.ask: the words write as a mixed fraction appear on the board
marks.list: the four multiplications appear one after the other
marks.end: a question mark appears after each one

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Multiply each of these, and then write the answer as a mixed fraction.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Seven times three fifths. Four times one third. Nine sevenths times six. Thirteen elevenths times six.
<bookmark mark='end'/>What are the four mixed fractions?

beats.on_screen: the four multiplications stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a bar cut into equal pieces; more pieces than one bar holds fill a second bar; full bars and the pieces left over are grouped as a mixed fraction

marks.bar: a bar cut into equal pieces appears
marks.more: extra pieces fill a second bar, then a third
marks.mixed: full bars and the left over pieces are grouped together

narration: <bookmark mark='bar'/>Picture a bar cut into equal pieces, and a full bar is one whole.
<bookmark mark='more'/>When we have more pieces than one bar holds, we fill one bar after another.
<bookmark mark='mixed'/>The full bars and the pieces left over together make a mixed fraction.

marks.given: the first two multiplications are written in the working band
marks.rest: the last two multiplications are written below

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, we have four multiplications.
The first two are seven times three fifths, and four times one third.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The last two are nine sevenths times six, and thirteen elevenths times six.

beats.on_screen: To find: each answer as a mixed fraction

marks.find: the find line is written under the given lines

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find each answer as a mixed fraction.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, multiply seven by three fifths, the same way as the example in your book.
Seven times three is twenty one, so we have twenty one fifths.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Twenty one divided by five is four, with one left over.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, multiply four by one third.
Four times one is four, so we have four thirds.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Four divided by three is one, with one left over.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, nine sevenths times six is the same as six times nine sevenths.
Six times nine is fifty four, so we have fifty four sevenths.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Fifty four divided by seven is seven, with five left over.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, thirteen elevenths times six is the same as six times thirteen elevenths.
Six times thirteen is seventy eight, so we have seventy eight elevenths.
<bookmark mark='split'/>Seventy eight divided by eleven is seven, with one left over.

marks.check: the check lines begin to appear

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, check each answer by putting the full bars and the left over pieces back together.
<bookmark mark='ca'/>Five times four plus one is twenty one.
<bookmark mark='cb'/>Three times one plus one is four.
<bookmark mark='cc'/>Seven times seven plus five is fifty four.
<bookmark mark='cd'/>Eleven times seven plus one is seventy eight.

marks.pay: all four answers stay on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='a'/>Twenty one fifths is four and one fifth.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Four thirds is one and one third.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Fifty four sevenths is seven and five sevenths.
<bookmark mark='d'/>Seventy eight elevenths is seven and one eleventh.
<bookmark mark='pay'/>Four and one fifth, one and one third, seven and five sevenths, seven and one eleventh.
